title: WP Super Cache Troubleshooting
description: Fix stale cached pages, cache not generating, logged-in user issues, and conflicts with other optimization plugins.

steps.title: Identify Cache Symptom
steps.instructions: Determine if pages show stale content, cache never builds, only anonymous users affected, or admin breaks. Note if another cache plugin is also active.

steps.title: Disable Duplicate Caching Plugins
steps.instructions: Run only one full-page cache (WP Super Cache, LiteSpeed, W3 Total Cache, etc.). Deactivate others to avoid double-caching and unpredictable purges.

steps.title: Verify mod_rewrite and Advanced Cache Drop-in
steps.instructions: Check Settings → WP Super Cache: mod_rewrite rules in .htaccess or wp-cache-config.php. Confirm advanced-cache.php exists in wp-content and WP_CACHE is true in wp-config.

steps.title: Review Rejected URI and Cookie Rules
steps.instructions: Ensure cart, checkout, my-account, and wp-admin are excluded. Add cookies that should bypass cache (woocommerce_items_in_cart, wordpress_logged_in).

steps.title: Fix or Disable Broken Preload
steps.instructions: Preload can hammer the server or serve incomplete pages. Disable preload temporarily, delete cache, and test manual cache generation on a single URL.

steps.title: Confirm Cache Purge on Publish
steps.instructions: After publishing, confirm the live page updates. If not, manually delete cache from the admin bar and check if a theme or plugin blocks wp_cache_clear_cache hooks.

steps.title: Check CDN and minify Conflicts
steps.instructions: Disable WP Super Cache minify if using Autoptimize or host CDN. CDN caching another layer may require purge rules at Cloudflare or similar.

steps.title: Verify Cache Headers and Fresh Content
steps.instructions: Use curl -I or DevTools to confirm cache HIT/MISS behavior. Test logged-out view after edits; confirm WooCommerce cart still works when caching is on.
